title: Dual-Use Research Oversight Gaps
bottleneck: Research with both beneficial and harmful applications (gain-of-function virology, AI capabilities, synthetic biology) lacks consistent oversight: rules vary by country, enforcement is patchy, and much work happens outside any review framework. Scientists often do not recognize dual-use implications of their own work. Oversight regimes are national while research is global, so restrictions in one country simply move work elsewhere.
why_it_blocks: Ungoverned dual-use research creates catastrophic risks that no single lab's judgment can adequately price. A single lab's misjudgment can create risks borne by all of humanity.
current_state: The BWC lacks verification, AI has no equivalent regime at all, and DURC policies cover only a slice of relevant work. International harmonization of dual-use oversight has barely begun. Harmonized international oversight is the only regime that can actually work.
